report: The patient's stridor, increased work of breathing, and oxygen requirement are best explained by traumatic supraglottic injury from a fall. Falling with an e-cigarette in the mouth and exam showing severe supraglottic edema support this. CT showed glottic/supraglottic swelling without fractures, and laryngoscopy revealed edema/sloughing worst at the epiglottis, consistent with localized impact injury. No fever or infectious prodrome argues against infection.
answer: Chemical burns of the pharynx and esophagus due to e-cigarette injury

report: Stridor, increased work of breathing, oxygen need, diffuse supraglottic edema on exam, CT glottic/supraglottic swelling without fracture, and laryngoscopic edema with mucosal sloughing confirm acute supraglottic edema. History of falling with e-cigarette in mouth and absent infectious features favor thermal/chemical airway injury over infectious epiglottitis. Leading diagnosis: acute supraglottic edema due to e-cigarette airway injury. Bronchoscopy/inflammatory markers pending don't change this.
answer: Chemical burns of the pharynx and esophagus due to e-cigarette injury
